title: The Throw-In (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational absurdist 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal football comedy mundane
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The throw-in is the most underrated moment in football
It happens approximately forty times a game
And approximately forty times a game
Everyone treats it as an inconvenience
Between the parts that actually matter

[Verse 2]
But the throw-in is a restart
A tiny restart
A moment where possession is assigned by geography
Not by merit
The ball went out near you
So now it is yours
To do something with
That is almost certainly less than what you hoped

[Chorus]
The throw-in says — here you go
The throw-in says — your turn
The throw-in says — both feet on the ground
Both hands on the ball
Both feet on the ground
The throw-in is very specific about the feet

[Bridge]
Chas said — the throw-in specialist is a myth
Every team has one player who gets given the long throws
One player who practised in the car park after training
One player who can reach the six-yard box from the touchline
And uses this ability with the enthusiasm of a person
Who has finally found their purpose

[Verse 3]
The beautiful game stops for the throw-in
Takes a breath
Someone picks up the ball
Someone steps back
Two feet on the line
And football begins again
From almost nothing
As it always has

[Outro]
The throw-in
The throw-in
That's my boy
